nba_directive.reason_text: Client wants to wait, but with a 7.25% rate there's a quantifiable gap to today's market that can be anchored immediately — pairing that math with a pinned callback prevents the conversation from going cold rather than letting a vague 'later' kill the deal.
nba_directive.recommended_strategy_text:
- Open by anchoring their exact rate and the gap to today's achievable rate
  - State their current rate plainly: 7.25% on a $278,030 balance at $1,965/mo P&I
  - Pull today's best qualifying rate for their scenario and show the new estimated P&I side-by-side
  - Express the monthly delta in real dollars (compute and present this — do not guess)

- Counter 'I want to wait for rates to drop' with break-even math, not a pitch
  - Calculate closing costs for this loan and divide by the monthly savings to produce a break-even month count
  - Point out: if they wait and rates drop further, they can refinance again — the 'you can always refi again later' reframe removes the fear of locking in too early
  - Make the cost of waiting tangible: every month at 7.25% vs. the lower rate is a specific dollar amount they are leaving on the table

- Tie the scenario to their stated life goal
  - Ask directly what the monthly savings would go toward (retirement contributions, debt payoff, a specific milestone)
  - Reframe the refi not as a rate transaction but as the mechanism that funds that goal starting on a specific date

- Honor the delay but make it concrete — pin a callback, do not leave it open-ended
  - Agree to their timeline explicitly, then name a specific date and time for a 10-minute callback
  - Confirm the callback via text immediately so it is on record
  - Set a personal reminder to follow up one day before the pinned date

- Do not repeat an equity or cash-out angle — this is a rate-and-term refinance conversation only

generated_sms: Hi there, totally understand wanting to wait on the credit side. Just so you know, your 7.25% rate costs you real dollars every month compared to what's available now-even if you refi again later, you're still saving in the meantime. Want to run the math when you're ready?
